title: Grill — one Select Projects control for New Task
summary:
Before the plan: **6 decisions** that change the shape of the build, plus **8 defaults** I'd bet on. Start with **Q1** — where the per-project Branch / Pull / Fetch rows live. It is the only answer that decides whether `SearchSelect` needs a portal: every picker popover is `position: absolute`, and the dialog's list is a `max-h-72 overflow-y-auto` box, so branch rows inside that list are clipped.

I've read the code and the prior investigation, so settled facts are below instead of being asked. The whole change is webview-only: no server, schema, migration or route change.

Source: the task text + screenshot (outside the repo). The committed contract this supersedes is `docs/specs/multi-repo-tasks.md:126-129` and `docs/plans/multi-repo-tasks-grill.md:39` (decision 16).

proven.text: **The combined control replaces both old selectors; there is no third path.** New Task renders a single `ProjectPicker`, then `WorktreeOptions`, then a `Repositories` block whose only 2+ entry is “Use multiple repositories…”. The ask removes that split.

**No server, schema, migration or route change.** `/projects/branches`, `/projects/fetch`, `/projects/pull` and `/projects/repo-root` already exist, and `BranchPicker` already calls the first three for any `workdir`.

**Exactly one selection must keep the old payload shape.** A 1-entry `repositories` array is rejected when the path is not a git repository, so a plain folder with Isolate off must still send `workdir` + top-level `baseRef`.

evidence.label: non-git path rejected

proven.text: **Count and forced Isolate must use the git-root-deduped set.** Two subdirectories of one repository collapse to one repository at create time, so a raw checkbox count would claim “2 projects” and disable Isolate for a single-repo task.

evidence.label: create decides multi after dedupe
evidence.code:
const keptRepositories = resolvedSet && resolvedSet.ok ? resolvedSet.repositories : [];
  const multiRepo = keptRepositories.length > 1;

proven.text: **This supersedes documented decisions.** The spec says one repo keeps the inline fields and 2+ uses the dialog; the architecture doc repeats it. Both must be amended in the same change, per `CLAUDE.md:5`.

evidence.label: spec UI section
evidence.code: - One shared `Repositories` dialog is used by the New Task panel and `CreateTaskFromIssueDialog`.

evidence.label: superseded decision 16
evidence.code: | 16 | UI | … A shared `Repositories` dialog … instead of per-repo rows in the New Task panel; with one repo, today's inline branch/base fields stay. |

proven.text: **e2e is the only coverage.** No unit test renders `NewTaskForm`; 11 specs drive the ProjectPicker trigger and 2 clone specs use its footer. A UI-only change that never wires base refs into the create payload stays green in `bun test`.

sections.title: Shape of the control
sections.intro: These decide the component architecture, the create payload and every e2e locator.

questions.title: Where do the per-project Branch / Pull / Fetch rows live, and in what order?
questions.why: This is the only answer that changes component architecture: rows in the dialog need a portal/fixed popover, rows inline do not. It also decides every e2e locator.
questions.context: The ask says the button goes “on top of the Isolate checkbox” and that every selected project gets the branch picker + Pull + Fetch that one project has today. Those two statements pull in different directions: today one Branch picker sits above Isolate (`WorktreeOptions.tsx:315-345`), while 2+ projects hide it and read base refs from the dialog's free-text inputs (`RepositoriesDialog.tsx:229-241`). Three layouts fit; the two inline ones differ only in whether the button sits immediately above Isolate (literal reading) or above the per-project rows (today's Project → Branch → Isolate order).

evidence.label: one Branch picker, hidden for multi
2+ uses free-text refs in the dialog
every picker popover is absolute
evidence.code: "absolute left-0 right-0 z-50 overflow-hidden rounded-md border border-border bg-card text-card-foreground shadow-xl",

options.label: Inline: button → branch rows → Isolate → Branch name
options.description: One Branch row per selected project directly under the Select Projects button; Isolate and the shared Branch name follow.
options.consequence: Keeps today's Project → Branch → Isolate order; base refs always visible; no portal work; the dialog drops its per-repo text input; the form grows with N.

options.label: Inline: button → Isolate → branch rows → Branch name
options.description: The button sits immediately above Isolate; the per-project rows come after it.
options.consequence: Most literal reading of “on top of the Isolate checkbox”; the refs that feed isolation appear below the toggle.

options.label: Inside the Select Projects dialog: form is button → Isolate → Branch name
options.description: Every selected project's Branch / Pull / Fetch row is configured inside the dialog.
options.consequence: Compact form, but `SearchSelect` must gain a portal/fixed mode (its popover is absolute inside a `max-h-72 overflow-y-auto` list); base refs are invisible when the dialog is closed.

recommendation.reason: Branch is a property of the selected projects, so it belongs inside the project block; this keeps today's field order and needs no popover rework.

questions.title: Does the selection apply on Save, or immediately on every toggle?
questions.why: Git-root dedupe and the same-root base-ref conflict are currently enforced on Save; a live surface has to run them on every toggle.
questions.context: The existing dialog resolves roots and merges on Save (`RepositoriesDialog.tsx:146-177`), and Save is disabled at zero. `MultiSearchSelect` applies each toggle immediately (`multi-search-select.tsx:110-113`). Either can back the new control; the difference is when dedupe runs and whether Cancel can abandon an edit.

evidence.label: the live multi-select precedent

options.label: Save / Cancel boundary (today's dialog)
options.consequence: Git-root dedupe and base-ref conflicts stay on one code path; Cancel and Escape abandon; one extra click per selection.

options.label: Apply every toggle immediately
options.consequence: Count updates live and there is no Save click, but dedupe/conflict checks become async on every toggle and there is no Cancel.

recommendation.reason: The dedupe and conflict rules already live on Save and are load-bearing; moving them live adds async states with no user-facing gain.

questions.title: Does the combined control apply to the issue dialog too, or only New Task?
questions.why: Both surfaces share `WorktreeOptions` and `RepositoriesDialog`; changing one and not the other means a mode flag, a fork, or a stale parity claim.
questions.context: `CreateTaskFromIssueDialog` renders the same `WorktreeOptions` (`:414`) and the same `RepositoriesDialog` (`:428-450`), with the issue's repo locked first (`:436`). `docs/architecture/issue-tasks.md:19` says the dialog sends worktree fields “exactly like the panel”. Its “discard this draft?” check reads `wt.baseRefDirty` (`:214-221`), which stops being the whole truth once every repo owns a ref.

evidence.label: dirty check reads one base ref
evidence.code:
const draftDirty =
    promptDirty ||
    references.length > 0 ||
    typeDirty ||
    !wt.isolate ||
    wt.baseRefDirty ||

options.label: Both surfaces; the issue's repo stays locked first
options.consequence: Keeps the shared component and the parity doc true; the issue dialog's dirty check must be rewired to see every ref.

options.label: New Task only
options.consequence: The shared dialog needs a 1+-selection mode for New Task and a 2+ mode for the issue dialog (or a fork); amend the parity claim.

recommendation.reason: Same component, same contract, and leaving one surface behind is exactly the drift the architecture doc warns about.

questions.title: “One selection is required” — what happens when the user tries to deselect the last project?
questions.why: Decides whether the dialog can hold an empty draft and how switching a single project works.
questions.context: I read this as **at least one**, not exactly one, because the same ask describes 2+ behavior; if you meant exactly one, the multi path disappears. Today the dialog allows zero but disables Save (`RepositoriesDialog.tsx:282`), the form requires `repos.length > 0` (`NewTaskForm.tsx:646-648`), and the picker auto-selects a project on open (`ProjectPicker.tsx:67-76`).

evidence.label: Save disabled at zero
evidence.code: <Button size="sm" onClick={() => void save()} disabled={busy || draft.length === 0}>

evidence.label: form requires at least one
evidence.code:
const canSubmit =
    title.trim() && prompt.trim() && workdir.trim() && repos.length > 0 && wt.valid

options.label: Allow zero in the draft; Save disabled with a “select at least one” hint
options.consequence: Switching one project is uncheck-old-then-check-new; the saved form never holds zero because Save cannot apply it.

options.label: Prevent unchecking/removing the last project
options.consequence: Guarantees at least one everywhere, but switching a single selection requires checking the new one first.

recommendation.reason: Today's dialog already behaves this way; blocking the last uncheck makes the common “replace one project” flow awkward.

questions.title: What exactly does the button say for 1 and for 2+ selected projects?
questions.why: This is the button's accessible name and every e2e locator; it also decides whether the form shows a count at all for one project.
questions.context: The ask says the number must show “just like currently”. There are three current precedents: the single Project trigger shows the project's name (`ProjectPicker.tsx:117`), `MultiSearchSelect` shows `1 → label, N → “N selected”` (`multi-search-select.tsx:103-107`), and the 2+ summary shows `N repositories` (`NewTaskForm.tsx:889`). Only the last two contain a number.

evidence.label: multi-select trigger rule

options.label: 1 → project name; 2+ → “2 projects selected”
options.consequence: Keeps the informative single case; 2+ carries the count, and the noun “projects” matches the button.

options.label: 1 → “1 project selected”; 2+ → “N projects selected”
options.consequence: The number is always visible, but one project's name disappears from the trigger.

options.label: 1 → project name; 2+ → “N selected”
options.consequence: Matches the existing `MultiSearchSelect` component exactly; slightly terser.

options.label: 1 → project name; 2+ → “N repositories”
options.consequence: Matches today's 2+ summary; “repositories” is the older noun.

recommendation.reason: It follows the existing multi-select trigger convention while keeping the single case as informative as today.

questions.title: Do we keep a way to pin a tag or commit SHA per project?
questions.why: Replacing the 2+ dialog's free-text ref with a branch picker removes an input the server still supports.
questions.context: `BranchPicker` only picks an existing branch row (`BranchPicker.tsx:194-220`); it can render a custom value if one is already set, but offers no way to type one. The current 2+ dialog has a free-text `Base ref (default HEAD)` input (`RepositoriesDialog.tsx:229-236`), and the server accepts any ref. The single-project picker has never offered tag/SHA entry.

evidence.label: free-text ref only in the 2+ dialog
evidence.code:
<Input
                      value={entry.baseRef ?? ""}
                      onChange={(e) => setBaseRef(path, e.target.value)}
                      placeholder="Base ref (default HEAD)"

evidence.label: BranchPicker lists branch rows only
evidence.code: const items: { value: string; label: string; hint: string; pinned: boolean }[] = [];

options.label: Branch rows only (parity with the single project)
options.consequence: One control per project and a smaller change; tag/SHA pinning remains available only through the API/CLI.

options.label: Branch picker + a small custom-ref input per row
options.consequence: Keeps today's 2+ capability; one extra control and validation path per selected project.

recommendation.reason: The ask is “the branch picker, Pull and Fetch we have for one project”; tag/SHA was never part of that row, and the API/CLI escape hatch stays.

sections.title: Confirm or override
sections.intro: Defaults I'd bet on. One click each; override any you disagree with.

questions.title: Auto-select the most recently added project when the form opens with nothing selected
questions.context: Today's `ProjectPicker` does this (`ProjectPicker.tsx:67-76`), and several e2e specs register a project and type a prompt without selecting one. If overridden: the form opens with “Select projects…” and Create stays disabled until a pick, and those specs need an explicit selection.

recommendation.reason: It makes the form valid on open and avoids an extra click for the returning user.

questions.title: When a 2+ selection drops back to one project, what happens to Isolate?
questions.context: Today an effect force-sets it true for 2+ (`NewTaskForm.tsx:268-270`). Restoring the previous value would make the task's layout change without a visible action.

recommendation.reason: No silent layout change; the user can uncheck it deliberately.

questions.title: Per-project Pull/Fetch exactly as today, with no “Pull all” / “Fetch all”
questions.context: Each button already mutates the user's source checkout (`BranchPicker.tsx:123-159`). With N rows there are N possible network operations before creation; the per-row spinner and error behavior are already built.

recommendation.value: Per-row Pull/Fetch only; no bulk action
recommendation.reason: The ask asks for the per-project controls; a bulk action is new scope with partial-failure states.

questions.title: Dialog affordances: search, the three management actions, and the zero-project state
questions.context: `ProjectPicker`'s footer is the only entry for Clone repository and Import sessions (`ProjectPicker.tsx:118-148`), its search is the only way to find a project by name, and the new button must be able to register the first project. `RepositoriesDialog` already owns “Add folder” and the native picker (`:124-139`).

recommendation.value: Add a search filter; move Browse for folder / Clone repository / Import sessions into the dialog; keep the button enabled even with no projects registered
recommendation.reason: All three footer actions need a home once `ProjectPicker` is retired, and the button is the only way to add the first project.

questions.title: How each per-project row is identified, and how a project is removed
questions.context: Today the dialog's row shows the name plus path (`RepositoriesDialog.tsx:223-224`) and a trash button that toggles the same selection (`:242-252`).

recommendation.value: Rows read “Branch · <project name>” (path added when two names collide); removal happens only in the Select Projects dialog — no per-row X
recommendation.reason: The button only shows a count for 2+, so the row label must name the project; keeping selection in one place avoids two paths mutating the same state.

questions.title: One shared Branch name for all projects, previewed from the first selected project's naming config
questions.context: The server anchors the shared name on the first kept repository (`orchestrator.ts:12551`) and reads that project's config (`12807`). If per-project branch names are wanted instead, that is a server/schema change (a branch per `repositories[]` entry) and rewrites the launch-prompt and PR docs. This is not a “primary repo” in the model (prior decision 13).

recommendation.value: One shared field; the preview uses the first selected project's `branchConfig`; the server applies one name with a per-repo `-N` fallback
recommendation.reason: The server already behaves this way, so the preview matches what will be created without a contract change.

questions.title: The button count and the forced Isolate both use the git-root-deduped set
questions.context: Two subdirectories of one repo create a single-repo task, so counting checked paths would disable Isolate and claim “2 projects” for a one-repo create (`orchestrator.ts:12513-12514`). The dialog already dedupes on Save and shows the note (`RepositoriesDialog.tsx:276`); the form sees the saved, deduped list.

recommendation.value: Yes — count what the server will create, and keep the “(some share a git root)” note
recommendation.reason: The count and the Isolate decision must not lie about a single-repo create.

questions.title: After creating a task, keep the whole project selection for the next task
questions.context: Today the form deliberately keeps `workdir` and does not reset `repos` after submit (`NewTaskForm.tsx:713-721`); rapid-fire task creation is the stated workflow.

recommendation.value: Keep every selected project (and each branch ref) for the next task
recommendation.reason: It preserves today's “same project for the next task” behavior and the rapid-fire workflow.
